title: The grown torus reads distance by freezing at every stage, and plainly only as a ladder
claim: For networks of equally spaced rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts grown by the band law (a loop of n rings, the n x 2 ladder, then the n x m tori), each stage read as a fixed network: (1) every stage reads the cut length D and the time length g*delta + 1 exactly, and on the ladder and tori D = ceil(delta/2); (2) every square torus whose lattice holds (0,2) or (2,0), the n x 2 ladder and its twisted forms, is on time for every n >= 2 (the plain first need comes at the time length for every ring and contact); (3) the n x m torus with 2 <= n <= m is on time exactly when n = 2 or n = m = 3, so every stage from the second band on is late but 3 x 3; (4) ring balls on the n x m torus are sum_b min(n, 2(r - |b|) + 1), on the cylinder 2r^2 + 2r + 1 up to r = (n - 1)/2 and then 2n more per step, and the time length's balls at radius 2r are the ring balls of radius r about the contact's two rings. Computed: on every square torus to index 100, triangular to 80 and honeycomb to 50, the ladders, the square tori holding (2,1) or a rotation of it, and the triangular tori holding a vector of length sqrt 3 are all on time, and every other on-time torus has index at most 17, 21 or 9; this corrects PLAIN-TIME-20261108-001B, Theorem 4, which holds for the rotation-invariant tori only.
failure_conditions: A stage of band growth with twin corners, or an isolated shortest route arriving at another lag than g*delta + 1.
A square torus holding (0,2) or (2,0) with a late ring.
An n x m torus with 3 <= n <= m, other than 3 x 3, that is on time.
A ring ball of the n x m torus or the cylinder that differs from the closed form.
foundation_claim_scope: Networks of rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts made by the band law, each stage read as a fixed network (A42); the freeze readings (A38, A40, A41) and the plain first need against the directed distance; tori of every shape for the census; two-time knots only (A30). The (2,1) and sqrt 3 tubes are computed to index 100 and 80.
